{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative bias (e.g., -0.25 or below) to counteract overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early stages of downward sentiment trends; model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts.",
    "When true outcomes show strong mean reversion (e.g., prices dropping after peaks), reduce forecasted peaks by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.",
    "In periods with sustained negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast.",
    "For long-term horizons (>15 days), apply a mild downward correction if recent history shows persistent underperformance (e.g., 3+ consecutive underforecasted days).",
    "If sentiment history includes a recent spike (e.g., 0.50 or 0.67), reduce forecasted peak by 10–15% to avoid overestimating momentum.",
    "When true outcomes are consistently higher than forecasts (e.g., >10% over 3+ days), apply a 5–10% upward bias to correct for underestimation.",
    "In cases where model forecasts are consistently too high (e.g., >75% of 30-day forecast exceeds true outcome), apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to align with historical mean."
  ]
}
